![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251721/assets/13fc8ff564a7162c556d050a10df6e8f23c0fca269e3b88168ca6681be3ad3a3.png)

Consider the picture above. Find a unit vector $u$ that is parallel to  $p+q$ and has the same direction as $p+q.$ 

Type $p$ and $q$ to represent the vectors $p$ and $q,$ respectively.  

$u=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we have to find $p+q.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $p+q$ goes from the tail of $p$ to the head of $q:$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251721/assets/68c14ce5ff66272986e958f09f30289d56519e90b34fae23362753f84c042a50.png)

In $△AHB$, we have $∠AHB={90}^{∘}$, $AH=2$ and $BH=3.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem gives

$$
\begin{aligned}|p+q| & =AB \\  & =\sqrt{A{H}^{2}+B{H}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9} \\  & =\sqrt{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the magnitude of $p+q$ is $\sqrt{13}.$ Consequently, the unit vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{1}{|p+q|}\cdot (p+q) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}(p+q).\end{aligned}
$$
